observations: Photo 0 shows a large flat-screen TV displaying the LG webOS interface.
Text 'webOS' and 'LG Gallery+' are clearly visible on the screen in photo 0.
Photo 1 shows the same TV displaying a high-definition landscape image.
Both photos contain a watermark that reads 'POSTED ON JIJI HARRY LAN'.
The TV is wall-mounted against a marble-effect wall panel.

claims.evidence: No physical scale or manufacturer label is visible to confirm dimensions.
The model number is not visible in the provided photos.
Resolution cannot be verified from compressed remote photos.
Photo 0 explicitly shows the LG webOS interface and LG-branded apps.

risks.risk: The photos may be stolen from another listing (indicated by the watermark).
risks.proof: A photo of the TV with a handwritten note showing the current date and buyer's name.

risks.risk: The screen may have hidden defects like dead pixels or vertical lines.
risks.proof: A close-up video of the screen displaying a solid white or grey background.

risks.risk: The internal hardware or ports may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the back ports and the TV successfully playing media from an external source.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the white sticker on the back of the TV showing the model and serial number.
A photo of the TV with a handwritten note of today's date and my name next to the screen.
A video of the TV being turned on and navigating through the settings menu.
response.reason: The seller's text is self-contradictory, claiming the brand is LG in the specifications but Samsung in the description. Additionally, the photos carry a 'HARRY LAN' watermark from the Jiji platform, which is a common sign of stolen images used in fraudulent listings.
